paragraphs: The falchion is a sword shaped like a tool. Weight forward, single edged and closer to a cleaver than to a duelling blade, it was cheap to make and effective in a way that embarrassed better bred weapons.

The model is light at 13,066 polygons and 13,072 vertices, built in quads only with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 8 maps all at 4096x4096, and supplied with the sheath. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits game weapons and characters, historical and fantasy film props, museum material, concept art and editorial illustration. On sale since 2017.

A throwing axe has to leave the hand cleanly and rotate predictably, which puts the mass in the head and almost nothing in the handle. Fantasy versions exaggerate the head enormously, and that is precisely what makes them read as fantasy.
The model is extremely light at 3,929 polygons and 3,930 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 5 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries StemCell certification.
At $29 it suits game weapons and characters, fantasy film and animation props, concept art, tabletop illustration and editorial work. On sale since 2021.

Pasta boxes have a window for one reason: the shape is the product. Farfalle, penne and fusilli cook differently and hold sauce differently, and the customer is buying a decision about the meal rather than a commodity.
The model is light at 20,523 polygons and 20,169 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $29 it suits packaging and label mockups, food and retail visualisation, e-commerce imagery, kitchen scenes, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Fast food seating is designed to be comfortable for about twenty minutes. The bench is hard, the table is fixed to the floor, and the whole arrangement is calculated around turnover rather than around lingering.
The model is extremely light at 4,454 polygons and 4,723 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, so a whole dining room costs almost nothing. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $29 it suits restaurant and interior visualisation, hospitality presentation, furniture marketing, film and television sets, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The shield and the credential together are what make a badge mean anything; the metal alone is a prop. Film and television have made the object so familiar that most people would recognise it faster than any actual identification.
The model holds 34,279 polygons and 20,151 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in a closed configuration suited to close renders. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits film and television props, game assets, editorial and news illustration, character accessories and previsualisation. On sale since 2022.

A biometric lock replaces something you carry with something you are, and the interesting design problem is the failure case. Every one of them still has a keyhole or a keypad hidden somewhere, because fingers get wet, cut and cold.
The model is extremely light at 3,722 polygons and 3,869 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.

At $29 it suits product and security visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, architectural and interior scenes, smart home presentation, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.
A safe is rated by how long it resists rather than by whether it does. Fire ratings are in minutes at a stated temperature, and the entire product is an argument about how long help takes to arrive.
The model holds 133,660 polygons and 68,082 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits product and security visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, interior and storage scenes, advertising, film props and game environments. On sale since 2024.

A folded chair is the state it spends most of its life in. Carried, stacked in a boot, leaned against a wall: the geometry of the folded object matters more to the buyer than the geometry of the open one.
The model is light at 57,898 polygons and 30,008 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in blue and folded. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits outdoor and leisure visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, garage and camping scenes, film props and game environments. On sale since 2023.

A lure is designed to be wrong in a specific way. Fish are not fooled by accuracy, they respond to movement, flash and vibration, which is why the most effective lures often look like nothing that has ever swum.
The model is very light at 9,394 polygons and 9,489 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits product and outdoor visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, tackle and fishing scenes, game props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

The flat lay is a photographic convention that became a product requirement. Garments are now folded and creased specifically so they photograph correctly from directly above, because that is how most of them will ever be seen.
The model is light at 11,303 polygons and 11,600 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in grey. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a blue build is offered separately.
At $29 it suits apparel and retail visualisation, e-commerce and catalogue imagery, advertising, styling and interior scenes, and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

A speaker that floats is solving a problem the pool created. Waterproofing was the first step, buoyancy the second, and the shape that results is dictated by having to sit upright in moving water with the driver facing the sky.
The model is very light at 9,759 polygons and 9,997 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $29 it suits product and lifestyle visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, pool and outdoor scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The paper flour sack survives because paper breathes. Flour needs to lose moisture slowly rather than sweat inside plastic, and the multi ply construction is there to hold a heavy powder without splitting at the seam.
The model is extremely light at 4,189 polygons and 4,013 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits packaging and label mockups, food and retail visualisation, e-commerce imagery, kitchen and bakery scenes, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

Foil laminate does the opposite job to paper: it seals completely. Coffee, dried goods and anything that oxidises go into it, and the barrier is a metal layer thin enough to be measured in atoms sandwiched between plastic films.
The model is extremely light at 4,189 polygons and 4,013 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits packaging and label mockups, food and retail visualisation, e-commerce imagery, kitchen and pantry scenes, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

A shirt folded around a board with pins and a collar stiffener is not packaging, it is presentation. The shape is entirely artificial, nobody folds one that way at home, and it exists purely so the garment holds a rectangle on a shelf.
The model is light at 22,300 polygons and 23,130 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $29 it suits apparel and retail visualisation, e-commerce and catalogue imagery, shopfitting presentation, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.
